status: Proposed exterior visualization only. Not a CAD export; geometry, fit, structural strength and mobility are not validated by these images.

prompts:
Use case: product-mockup. Create a beautiful, photorealistic industrial-design studio render of the PROPOSED NEXT exterior revision of Tinfox, the compact four-legged robot in the two references.
Reference 1 is the established studio aesthetic and product identity; reference 2 is current CAD packaging, NOT a user interface to reproduce.
Retain recognizable proportions: compact narrow elongated body, four legs with approximately equal 170 mm upper and lower links, three actuators per leg clustered at the hip, underside dark battery cassette, low top lidar, a gently convex front camera face with two lenses. All four complete legs and feet must fit in frame.
UPDATE THE BODY: smoothly rounded warm off-white body shell enclosing the chassis and fixed roll motors, modest bevels blending into soft shoulders, no flat box-like torso. Show an articulated enclosure: graphite moving hip pods nest in deep rounded shoulder sockets, with narrow circular overlap seams around the hip-roll axes. Each pod encloses the hip-pitch motor and meets the thigh at a separate circular pitch seam. Hip roll and hip pitch are perpendicular axes, not a single rigid shoulder. Cover the motor stack compactly without swelling the body width. The head is supported from the chassis with a substantial integrated structure, no thin suspended straps. No decorative rear bridge, tail, fin or rear endcap. End the body cleanly at its functional enclosure.
UPDATE ALL FOUR LIMBS: structural warm off-white two-piece thighs, gently convex faces with flattened oval cross-sections, softly rounded leading/trailing edges, broad organic blend from circular proximal motor housing into a tapered thigh and compact knee. Graphite shins have smooth rounded flattened-oval cross-sections, a single gentle longitudinal curve, narrowing toward small black rubber feet. NO square channels, exposed rib grids, sharp plate-like long edges, S-shaped double curves, enormous ball joints or skinny decorative attachment stalks. Keep flat internal mating lands invisible inside. Make restrained assembly seams visible around each two-piece limb perimeter, a few recessed functional screws, robust bearing surrounds. Knee transmission is proximal-motor-driven by one straight pushrod, discreetly visible only in the inner/rear clearance channel; no belt, no motor at knee, no external decorative cables.
Composition: one coherent full robot, front three-quarter view at a slightly elevated camera angle, nose toward right, all four feet visible, relaxed planted stance, on warm light-gray seamless studio floor. Premium precision-instrument aesthetic: warm mineral off-white, graphite, brushed metal joint discs, tiny orange functional accents, only small lowercase 'tinfox' marking. Soft large-area studio lighting with clear shadows that reveal curved surfaces and joint separation. High-detail realistic matte polymer materials, no aggressive sci-fi styling.
This is an honest design concept, not a verified mechanical drawing. Include a small discreet caption in the lower left, exactly: 'TINFOX / ARTICULATED SHELL CONCEPT'. No other annotation, no dimension claims, no branded design references, no UI, no watermark.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Refine this exact Tinfox studio concept. Preserve the robot identity, four-leg stance, body packaging, camera face, underside batteries, articulated shoulder pods, composition, background and caption.
Make a visible, important change to the limbs: ALL FOUR GRAPHITE SHINS must have CLOSED, SMOOTH, STRONGLY CONVEX FLATTENED-OVAL CROSS-SECTIONS. Replace the current straight-edged inset channels, slots, ribs and flat rectangular faces with smooth continuous rounded shells, like a gently tapered ergonomic tool handle. Each shin has ONE gentle longitudinal curve, broad rounded leading/trailing edges, no S-bend. Show a fine longitudinal two-piece seam on the side, at most two small recessed screws, and a substantial compact rounded knee bearing housing merging smoothly into the oval shaft. The central outer shin face should catch a continuous curved highlight, visibly cylindrical/elliptical, never flat like a plate. No long decorative recesses or slots. Keep the shin slender, same length and position; do not turn it into a bulbous animal leg.
Also make the off-white thigh cross-sections more oval with stronger smooth crown across their outer faces and softly rounded side edges, while maintaining compact motor-root diameter and broad material around the knee. These are two structural shell halves with a restrained perimeter seam, not layered sheet-metal plates.
Retain clear circular pitch seams at the thigh root and a separate roll-carrier cuff at the body socket; do not fuse shoulders rigidly into the torso. No extra knees, no exposed motor on the knee, no belts, no decorative rear cap. Premium precision-instrument design and physically plausible matte polymer shading. Keep exact caption 'TINFOX / ARTICULATED SHELL CONCEPT'.

Use case: product-mockup. Create a companion close-up industrial-design render of the exact Tinfox robot shown in the reference. This is the proposed rounded limb and articulated body enclosure, not a fabrication drawing.
Composition: a landscape two-panel design-detail plate on a warm light-gray studio backdrop. Left panel about 60 percent width: show the front body corner and one complete attached front leg from the articulated shoulder socket through its knee to its rubber foot, at a clear three-quarter angle. Crop the rest of the robot intentionally, not the featured leg. Right panel about 40 percent width: a larger macro view of that SAME leg's knee and upper shin, viewed from a slightly different angle so the convex cross-section and subtle side seam are obvious. Maintain one consistent design across both panels. No exploded parts, no invented cutaway interior or extra hardware.
Preserve reference details: body-mounted convex camera face, warm off-white gently rounded body shell, graphite moving hip pod in rounded body socket, visible concentric overlap seam at the roll connection and separate pitch connection at thigh root. Actuators remain clustered at the shoulder, not at knee. The off-white structural thigh has a smooth flattened-oval section, curved outer crown, a quiet two-piece perimeter seam and a few recessed screws. Its round proximal housing transitions broadly and smoothly into the tapered thigh and compact knee. The graphite shin is a closed smooth tapered oval structural clamshell with a single gentle longitudinal curve and rounded leading/trailing edges, fine side seam, only two recessed fasteners. No flat rectangular shin panel, no long recessed slot or rib grid. Knee bearing housing and pushrod attachment root blend broadly into the shell. Keep an unobtrusive clearance opening behind the knee for the internal pushrod; do not add an exposed motor, belt, or complex linkage outside the limb. The macro panel must show a rounded knee transition and the shin's oval cross-section via soft flowing highlights, not a square rail.
Materials: fine matte polymer, graphite joint collars, subtle brushed-metal axle ends, tiny orange functional accents. High-end precision-instrument aesthetic, realistic soft studio illumination, sharp detail, gentle contact shadows, coherent anatomy and mechanical organization.
Use small neutral typography only: panel labels 'SHOULDER + LIMB' and 'KNEE + OVAL SHIN'; footer 'TINFOX / SURFACE AND SEAM CONCEPT'. No dimensions, no brand references, no claim of validated motion or manufacture, no UI, no watermark.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Correct ONLY the excessive crescent-shaped bow of the off-white upper thigh in the LEFT panel of this concept plate. Keep the shoulder and knee centers exactly where they are. The thigh's longitudinal centerline should follow the almost straight diagonal segment connecting these two joint centers. Make it a compact smoothly tapered flattened-oval limb, full and rounded at the circular motor root, narrowing steadily to the knee, with only subtle side-profile curvature. It must NOT look like a banana, crescent, hook, C-shape, or S-shape. Reduce the bulge on its left outline and fill the excessively scooped right outline so the middle of the thigh is centered on the line between the joints. Keep its smooth convex cross-section, fine two-piece seam, modest recessed screws, and original joint dimensions. Preserve EVERYTHING ELSE in both panels: graphite shins, body and shoulder, foot, lighting, background, right-hand knee close-up, text, panel layout. This is the same Tinfox limb design, with a clean nearly straight upper link and a gently curved lower link.
